lines: Right. Attack their fleet at sea,
or have your First Mate write
a declaration of war at the Guild.
Get a contract in a nearby town
right away. After that, you can
drive them out just by investing.
(Right! We could get a contract
even in a town another faction
controls completely!)
So helping troublemakers like us
would risk angering
the King of Spain?
That's world politics for you.
Kuhn is Spain's enemy, too,
so I can help you defeat him.
That's as far as my help goes.
The Patterned Cloth is the map
to the Proof of Conquest
in the Mediterranean, right?
I've looked and looked, but it
still doesn't look like a map.
Too dark to see.
Pass me that Brass Lamp.
I never thought
the heat from the Brass Lamp
would reveal the markings.
So that's how we were meant
to use the Brass Lamp.
Who would have guessed
the heat would reveal it?
Indeed. Quite good for an accident.
All right! We have the map.
Now we just have to find
the Proof of Conquest
in the Mediterranean!
I hear the Pope will back
the Portuguese Crown's claim
to rule again if we show him the
seven Proofs of Conquest you found.
In the King of Portugal's name,
you are now viceroy of the Estado,
all our overseas trade territories!
The fabled Muramasa blades carry
a curse said to bring ill fortune
to Tokugawa, ruler of Japan.
They are marked for destruction.
A clan that bears Tokugawa a grudge
seems to have hidden
one blade in East Asia. I thought
you should have word of it.
They should be working!
Demon-Piercing Arrow, indeed!
Oh, that's its name.
Rather grand, isn't it?
It makes you a master archer,
or so they say. The men
wonder if it works on cannons.
No one's tending the ship!
Cannon practice would do them more
good than all this idle chatter!
